questions.explanation:
It is given that, \(x_1=1.22 \mathrm{~mm}, x_2=1.23 \mathrm{~mm}\),
\[
\begin{gathered}
x_3=1.19 \mathrm{~mm} \text { and } x_4=1.20 \mathrm{~mm} \\
x_{\text {mean }}=\frac{x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4}{4}=\frac{1.22+1.23+1.19+1.20}{4}=1.21 \\

\left|\Delta x_4\right|=\left|x_{\text {mean }}-x_4\right|=|1.21-1.20|=0.01 \\

\% \text { error }=\frac{\Delta x_{\text {mean }}}{x_{\text {mean }}}=\frac{0.06}{4 \times 1.21} \times 100=\frac{150}{121} \%
\end{gathered}
\]

Comparing above result with \(\frac{x}{121} \%\), we get \(x=150\).

Let \(R _1=\{(a, b) \in N \times N :|a-b| \leq 13\}\) and \(R _2=\{(a, b) \in N \times N :|a-b| \neq 13\}\). Then on \(N\), which of the following is true? 

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 June (Shift 2)]
options: \(R_1\) is an equivalence relation but \(R_2\) is not
\(R_2\) is an equivalence relation but \(R_1\) is not
questions.explanation:
For \(R_1\):

Reflexive:

\((a, a) \in R_1\) because \(|a-a|=0 \leq 13\)

Symmetric:

if \((a, b) \in R_1\), then \(|a-b| \leq 13 \Rightarrow|b-a| \leq 13\), so \((b, a) \in R_1\)

Transitive fails: take \(a=1, b=14, c=27\)

Then \(|1-14|=13\) and \(|14-27|=13\), so \((1,14) \in R_1\) and \((14,27) \in R_1\)

but \(|1-27|=26>13\), so \((1,27) \notin R_1\)

Hence \(R_1\) is not an equivalence relation

For \(R_2\):

Reflexive: \((a, a) \in R_2\) because \(|a-a|=0 \neq 13\)

Symmetric:

If \((a, b) \in R_2\), then \(|a-b| \neq 13 \Rightarrow|b-a| \neq 13\), so \((b, a) \in R_2\)

Transitive fails: take \(a=1, b=3, c=14\)

Then \(|1-3|=2 \neq 13\) and \(|3-14|=11 \neq 13\), so \((1,3) \in R_2\) and \((3,14) \in R_2\)

but \(|1-14|=13\), so \((1,14) \notin R_2\)

Hence \(R_2\) is not an equivalence relation.

Therefore, neither \(R_1\) nor \(R_2\) is an equivalence relation.

Let \( f: R \rightarrow R \) be continuous function satisfying \( f(x)+f(x+k)=n \), for all \( x \in R \) where \( k>0 \) and \( n \) is a positive integer. If \( I_{1}=\int_{0}^{4 n k} f(x) d x \) and \( I_{2}=\int_{-k}^{3 k} f(x) d x \), then

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 June (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Given \(f(x)+f(x+k)=n\).

Replacing \(x\) by \(x+k\), we get

\(f(x+k)+f(x+2k)=n\).

Subtracting both equations,

\(f(x)-f(x+2k)=0\).

Therefore \(f(x+2k)=f(x)\).

So \(f\) is periodic with period \(2k\).

Now \(\int_a^{a+2k}f(x)\,dx=\int_a^{a+k}f(x)\,dx+\int_{a+k}^{a+2k}f(x)\,dx\).

In the second integral, put \(x=t+k\), then

\(\int_{a+k}^{a+2k}f(x)\,dx=\int_a^{a+k}f(t+k)\,dt\).

So \(\int_a^{a+2k}f(x)\,dx=\int_a^{a+k}\{f(t)+f(t+k)\}\,dt\).

Since \(f(t)+f(t+k)=n\), we get \(\int_a^{a+2k}f(x)\,dx=\int_a^{a+k}n\,dt=nk\).

Now \(I_1=\int_0^{4nk}f(x)\,dx\).

Length of interval \(=4nk\), and period length \(=2k\).

Number of complete periods \(=\frac{4nk}{2k}=2n\).

Therefore \(I_1=2n\cdot nk=2n^2k\).

Also \(I_2=\int_{-k}^{3k}f(x)\,dx\).

Length of interval \(=4k\), so number of complete periods \(=\frac{4k}{2k}=2\).

Therefore \(I_2=2\cdot nk=2nk\).

Now \(I_1+nI_2=2n^2k+n(2nk)=4n^2k\).

Let \(x=x(y)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(2 y e^{x / y^2} d x+\left(y^2-4 x e^{x / y^2}\right) d y=0\) such that \(x(1)=0\). Then, \(x(e)\) is equal to 

 

[JEE Main 2022, 28 June (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Given differential equation is \(2ye^{x/y^2}dx+\left(y^2-4xe^{x/y^2}\right)dy=0\).

Since \(x=x(y)\), we write \(dx=\frac{dx}{dy}dy\).

So, \(2ye^{x/y^2}\frac{dx}{dy}+y^2-4xe^{x/y^2}=0\).

Let \(x=vy^2\).

\(\frac{dx}{dy}=y^2\frac{dv}{dy}+2yv\).

 we get \(2ye^v\left(y^2\frac{dv}{dy}+2yv\right)+y^2-4vy^2e^v=0\).

So, \(2y^3e^v\frac{dv}{dy}+4y^2ve^v+y^2-4y^2ve^v=0\).

Therefore, \(2y^3e^v\frac{dv}{dy}+y^2=0\).

 \(2ye^v\frac{dv}{dy}+1=0\).

So, \(e^v\frac{dv}{dy}=-\frac{1}{2y}\).

Now, \(e^v\frac{dv}{dy}=\frac{d}{dy}(e^v)\).

Therefore, \(\frac{d}{dy}(e^v)=-\frac{1}{2y}\).

Integrating both sides, we get \(e^v=-\frac{1}{2}\log_e y+C\).

Since \(x(1)=0\), we have \(v=\frac{x}{y^2}=0\) at \(y=1\).

So, \(e^0=-\frac{1}{2}\log_e 1+C\).

Therefore, \(1=0+C\), hence \(C=1\).

Thus, \(e^v=1-\frac{1}{2}\log_e y\).

Since \(v=\frac{x}{y^2}\), we get \(e^{x/y^2}=1-\frac{1}{2}\log_e y\).

At \(y=e\), we get \(e^{x/e^2}=1-\frac{1}{2}\log_e e\).

So, \(e^{x/e^2}=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\).

 \(\frac{x}{e^2}=\log_e\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\).

Therefore, \(\frac{x}{e^2}=-\log_e 2\).

Hence, \(x(e)=-e^2\log_e 2\)

\(z+\overline{z}=iz^2+z^2\)

\(=2\)
